sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: John Washington grew up with his family's stories of migration and escape,
sentences.zh: 约翰·华盛顿从小听着家里关于迁徙和逃亡的故事长大，

sentences.en: from hiding in train compartments and swimming across rivers,
sentences.zh: 从躲在火车车厢里到横渡河流，

sentences.en: to the airplane his mother took to leave Romania for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 再到他母亲十几岁时为了离开罗马尼亚前往美国而乘坐的飞机。

sentences.en: as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 但这些独自在危险中摸索前行的故事，

sentences.en: But these stories of foraging out dangerously on your own,
sentences.zh: 在他看来，就像是遥远过去传说的故事。

sentences.en: they seemed to him like tales from a distant paSt.
sentences.zh: 但后来我记得我第一次亲身面对它的时候，

sentences.en: But then I remember when I first confronted it personally,
sentences.zh: 那是在21世纪初叶。

sentences.en: and that was in the mid-2000s.
sentences.zh: 约翰当时正和一位朋友在安扎-博雷戈沙漠露营，

sentences.en: John was on a camping trip with a friend out in the Anza-Borrego desert,
sentences.zh: 就在圣地亚哥以东。

sentences.en: just east of San Diego.
sentences.zh: 我是《99PI》的制作人拉什·梅丹，接下来的内容由我来讲述。

sentences.en: This is 99PI producer Lash Medan, and they're going to take it from here.
sentences.zh: 约翰和他的伙伴正开车行驶在一条土路上，寻找露营的地方。

sentences.en: John and his buddy were driving down a dirt road, looking for a place to camp.
sentences.zh: 我们看到一个年轻人从路肩走上路面，向我们招手示意停车。

sentences.en: And we saw a young man step into the road from his shoulder and flag us down.
sentences.zh: 当时，我几乎不会说西班牙语。

sentences.en: At that point, I didn't speak much Spanish at all.
sentences.zh: 我们试图沟通，最终明白他是一名移民。

sentences.en: We tried to communicate with each other, and we understood that he was a migrant.
sentences.zh: 我们也意识到自己身处何地，大约在边境墙以北15英里处，

sentences.en: And also realized where we were, which was about 15 miles north of the border wall,
sentences.zh: 地形非常崎岖。

sentences.en: over really rough terrain.
sentences.zh: 他显然非常口渴，身体状况也不太好。

sentences.en: And he was clearly very thirsty and not in great shape.
sentences.zh: 他们给了他一些水，还给他续了几次杯。

sentences.en: They gave him some water, topped him off a couple times.
sentences.zh: 那个人随后请求搭车去下一个城镇。

sentences.en: The man then asked for a ride to the next town.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，约翰不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: And in that moment, John didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道这是违法的，但我们并不真正了解

sentences.en: Because we knew that it was illegal, but we didn't really understand
sentences.zh: 如果被抓到会有什么后果，会发生什么。

sentences.en: the implications of if we were to be caught, of what would happen.
sentences.zh: 约翰知道根据联邦法律，

sentences.en: John knew that under federal law,
sentences.zh: 帮助无证移民进入美国是违法的。

sentences.en: it's illegal to help undocumented immigrants into the United States.
sentences.zh: 如果他载了这个人，他很可能会面临联邦指控。

sentences.en: And that if he gave this man a ride, there was a chance he'd face a federal offense.
sentences.zh: 所以他们祝他好运，然后回到车上，开车离开了。

sentences.en: So they wished him luck and went on their way, got back in their car, and drove off.
sentences.zh: 当我们到达营地开始卸货时，我想我突然意识到了什么。

sentences.en: And then when we got to camp and we started unpacking, I think it hit me.
sentences.zh: 我对我们所做的事情感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And I was kind of horrified by what we had done.
sentences.zh: 我说，天哪，我们把这个身体状况不佳的年轻人留在了路边。

sentences.en: And I said, oh my God, we left this young man who was in bad shape on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 于是我们跳回车里，开车回去试图找到他。

sentences.en: And so we jumped back in the car and we drove back to try to find him.
sentences.zh: 但我们没找到他。

sentences.en: And we didn't find him.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们没找到。

sentences.en: Of course we didn't.
sentences.zh: 在那之后的漫长岁月里，我逐渐意识到，

sentences.en: And in the years and long times since then, there's been this slow, dawning realization that
sentences.zh: 我的行为是非常不人道的。

sentences.en: I acted in a really inhumane way.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们现在构建社会的方式，

sentences.en: And yet the entire force of the way that we structure society right now,
sentences.zh: 尤其是在美国，以及其他许多地方，

sentences.en: especially in the United States, but many other places as well,
sentences.zh: 迫使我采取了那种行为。

sentences.en: was compelling me to act that way.
sentences.zh: 它将我定为罪犯，或者说，如果我为他提供所需的帮助，它就会将我定为罪犯。

sentences.en: It was criminalizing me, or would have criminalized me for offering him the help that he needed.
sentences.zh: 那一天让他明白，边境墙已经渗透进了他的脑海。

sentences.en: That day showed him that the border wall had seeped into his head.
sentences.zh: 是的，那堵墙，墙的逻辑，以及我们今天执行的移民逻辑，

sentences.en: Yeah, the wall, the logic of the wall, the logic of immigration as we enforce it today
sentences.zh: 已经深深植入我的脑海，以至于我没有提供帮助。

sentences.en: had gotten to my head so much such that I didn't provide help.
sentences.zh: 边境是一个如此强大的概念，以至于我们甚至不需要亲眼看到它，就会相信它或信仰它。

sentences.en: A border is an idea so powerful that we never even have to see it to believe it or believe in it.
sentences.zh: 全球边境可能是和平与冲突、暴力与庆祝、机遇与禁锢的场所。

sentences.en: Global borders can be sites of peace and conflict, violence and celebration, opportunity and confinement.
sentences.zh: 而现存的边境，即日益军事化且界限分明的边境，

sentences.en: And borders as they exist today, which is to say increasingly militarized and clearly defined,
sentences.zh: 实际上是一个相对较新的政治发明。

sentences.en: they're actually a relatively recent political invention.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪，严格控制的国界才开始在世界各地蔓延。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the 20th century that strictly controlled national borders started to spread around the world.
sentences.zh: 我自己的生活也深受边境的影响。

sentences.en: My own life has been shaped by borders.
sentences.zh: 一场暴力的边境形成将我的祖父母变成了难民。

sentences.en: A violent border formation turned my grandparents into refugees.
sentences.zh: 我自己也移民过两次。

sentences.en: I myself have immigrated twice.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了理解边境有时以奇怪且矛盾的方式运作，

sentences.en: And so, in an attempt to understand the weird and contradictory ways that borders sometimes operate,
sentences.zh: 我想和约翰谈谈。

sentences.en: I wanted to talk to John.
sentences.zh: 约翰是一位移民记者，也是《开放边境的理由》一书的作者。

sentences.en: John's an immigration reporter, and he's also the author of the book The Case for Open Borders.
sentences.zh: 在他的书中，约翰写到了世界各地不同的边境以及它们的运作方式。

sentences.en: In his book, John writes about different borders around the world and how they work.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天这期节目的主题。

sentences.en: And that's what our episode will be about today.
sentences.zh: 我们的第一站是1961年的柏林。

sentences.en: Our first stop is Berlin, 1961.
sentences.zh: 从1961年到1989年，柏林墙将东柏林和西柏林隔开。

sentences.en: From 1961 to 1989, the Berlin Wall separated East and West Berlin.
sentences.zh: 关于柏林墙，再多说一点背景。

sentences.en: So, a little bit of more context about the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 1961年刚开始建造时，这堵墙的官方名称是“反法西斯防卫墙”。

sentences.en: The official name of the wall when it was first starting to be built in 1961 was the Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart.
sentences.zh: 这道著名的混凝土屏障，顶部装有铁丝网，配有岗楼和地雷，

sentences.en: This famous concrete barrier, topped with barbed wire, guarded with watchtowers and mines,
sentences.zh: 是由共产主义东德建造的，旨在保护其领土免受西德人的侵害。

sentences.en: it was built by communist East Germany to protect their territory from the West Germans.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果有人了解柏林墙，它实际上是为了阻止人们向另一个方向走。

sentences.en: And yet, if anyone knows anything about the Berlin Wall, it was really stopping people from going the other direction.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点值得注意，墙往往会产生与预期相反的效果。

sentences.en: I think that's an interesting thing to note, that walls often have the opposite effect that they are purported to have.
sentences.zh: 如果你深入回顾历史，最初的边境划分并不是为了把人挡在外面，

sentences.en: And if you look back deep into history, the very first sort of border demarcations weren't to keep people out,
sentences.zh: 而是为了把人关在里面。

sentences.en: but they were to keep people in.
sentences.zh: 柏林墙也不例外。

sentences.en: The Berlin Wall was no exception.
sentences.zh: 这变得太困难了，简直太危险了。

sentences.en: It's become too difficult, simply too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 你看，你不需要跨越一堵墙，而是两堵。

sentences.en: You see, you don't have to cross one wall, but two.
sentences.zh: 在某些路段，甚至多达五堵。

sentences.en: And in some sections, as many as five.
sentences.zh: 三米高的混凝土墙。

sentences.en: Concrete, three meters high.
sentences.zh: 铁丝网围栏、路障、绊线。

sentences.en: Barbed wire fences, barricades, tripwires.
sentences.zh: 这堵墙还有另一个意想不到的后果。

sentences.en: There was also another unintended consequence of the wall.
sentences.zh: 直到为时已晚，人们才意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Something that people didn't realize until it was too late.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这堵墙正在让人患病。

sentences.en: The wall, it turned out, was making people sick.
sentences.zh: 有一位东德心理学家提出了“墙病”（mauerkronkite）这个词，

sentences.en: There is a concept that came out of an East German psychologist who coined the term mauerkronkite, or wall sickness,
sentences.zh: 这是他对这种将社会一分为二的想法如何潜入人们脑海的理解。

sentences.en: which is his understanding of how much this idea of cleaving a society in two creeped into people's heads.
sentences.zh: 它改变了人们对自己的看法。

sentences.en: And it changed the way that they thought about themselves.
sentences.zh: 它改变了人们思考和看待他人的方式。

sentences.en: It changed the way that they thought about and saw other people.
sentences.zh: 在柏林墙的两侧都发现了患有“墙病”的人。

sentences.en: Those affected with wall sickness were found on both sides of the Berlin Wall.
sentences.zh: 据心理学家称，部分原因是由于这堵墙，他们表现出抑郁、焦虑、自杀倾向和偏执的某种组合。

sentences.en: According to psychologists, partially because of the wall, they displayed some combination of depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation, and paranoia.
sentences.zh: 他们住得离墙越近，症状就越严重。

sentences.en: The closer they lived to the wall, the more acute their symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，柏林墙在1989年倒塌了。

sentences.en: So, the Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
sentences.zh: 我认为重要的一点是，它是如何倒塌的，我认为人们开始基本上看穿了它。

sentences.en: And I think one of the important things to recognize is how it fell is I think people started just basically seeing through it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们能够看穿边境的逻辑。

sentences.en: What I mean is they were able to see through the logic of the border.
sentences.zh: 这不是通过了一项法案或新法律。

sentences.en: It wasn't a bill that was passed or a new law that was passed.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是民众的不满和抗议。

sentences.en: It was just popular discontent and proteSt.
sentences.zh: 人们开始聚集，开始越过边境。

sentences.en: People just started gathering, just started crossing the border.
sentences.zh: 部分得益于大规模抗议和当时东德日益加剧的不稳定性，

sentences.en: Thanks in part to mass protest and the increasing instability in East Germany at the time,
sentences.zh: 边境的限制最终放宽了。

sentences.en: restrictions at the border eventually loosened.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1989年11月9日，东德政府在午夜前开放了边境。

sentences.en: Then, on November 9th, 1989, the East German government opened the border, just before midnight.
sentences.zh: 成千上万来自双方的德国人立即涌向柏林墙，

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of Germans from both sides immediately flocked to the wall,
sentences.zh: 要求将其拆除。

sentences.en: demanding that it be knocked down.
sentences.zh: 看看他们。

sentences.en: Take a look at them.
sentences.zh: 他们从昨晚就在那里了。

sentences.en: They've been there since last night.
sentences.zh: 他们成千上万地来到这里。

sentences.en: They are here in the thousands.
sentences.zh: 他们有几万人。

sentences.en: They are here in the tens of thousands.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，他们会高喊，

sentences.en: Occasionally, they shout,
sentences.zh: “墙必须倒下”（De Mao must veck），墙必须消失。

sentences.en: De Mao must veck, the wall must go.
sentences.zh: 当时，全世界大约有十几道国际边境墙。

sentences.en: At that point, there was around a dozen international border walls throughout the world.
sentences.zh: 那时人们对开放有着巨大的庆祝。

sentences.en: And there was a huge celebration of openness.
sentences.zh: 然而，从那以后，出现了一种巨大的倒退。

sentences.en: And yet, there's been an enormous retrenchment since then.
sentences.zh: 今天大约有80道边境墙。

sentences.en: There are somewhere around 80 border walls today.
sentences.zh: 它们正在被加固，变得越来越军事化。

sentences.en: They are being hardened, ever more militarized.
sentences.zh: 这是人类历史上边境墙数量最多的一次。

sentences.en: That's more border walls than ever before in human history.
sentences.zh: “墙病”通常指代那个时代。

sentences.en: And wall sickness is usually references just that era.
sentences.zh: 但我认为今天世界上许多其他地方都感染了“墙病”。

sentences.en: But I think that so many other places throughout the world today are infected with wall sickness.
sentences.zh: 世界各国都在与边境问题作斗争。

sentences.en: Countries worldwide have wrestled with borders.
sentences.zh: 在哪里设置边境，如何守卫它们。

sentences.en: Where to place them, how to guard them.
sentences.zh: 约翰写道，边境往往保护的是一个国家的理念，而不是国家本身。

sentences.en: And John writes that borders tend to protect the idea of a country more than the country itself.
sentences.zh: 也许是用铁丝网围栏或旗帜、安全检查站或岗楼。

sentences.en: Maybe it's with barbed wire fencing or a flag, a security checkpoint or a watchtower.
sentences.zh: 每个边境都有其独特的仪式感。

sentences.en: Each border comes with its own flavor of pageantry.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带到了第二站，拉德克利夫线。

sentences.en: Which brings us to our second stop, the Radcliffe Line.
sentences.zh: 在这里，在印度阿塔里和巴基斯坦瓦格赫镇之间的边境，有围栏，有警察。

sentences.en: Here at the border, between the towns of Atari, India and Vaga, Pakistan, there's fences, there's police.
sentences.zh: 还有冰淇淋和脸部彩绘。

sentences.en: There's also ice cream and face paint.
sentences.zh: 你可以买到嘉年华零食和印有小机枪图案的钥匙扣。

sentences.en: You can buy carnival snacks and keychains with little machine guns on them.
sentences.zh: 在边境大门的两侧，有两个巨大的体育场。

sentences.en: On either side of the border gate, there are two huge stadiuMs.
sentences.zh: 一个给印度人，另一个给巴基斯坦人。

sentences.en: One for Indians and the other for Pakistanis.
sentences.zh: 自1959年以来，两国士兵每天都在这里举行精心设计的仪式。

sentences.en: Since 1959, soldiers from both countries have staged an elaborate ceremony here.
sentences.zh: 每天同一时间。

sentences.en: At the same time, every single day.
sentences.zh: 这是一种编排好的舞蹈对决。

sentences.en: It's a sort of choreographed dance battle.
sentences.zh: 他们像求偶的鸟儿一样昂首阔步。

sentences.en: They strut back and forth like birds doing a mating call.
sentences.zh: 他们每天都表演这个仪式。

sentences.en: Every day, they perform this ceremony.
sentences.zh: 他们互相展示肌肉。

sentences.en: They flex their muscles at each other.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至对着对方咆哮。

sentences.en: They literally growl at each other.
sentences.zh: 他们进行这种类似鹅步的行进，高抬腿向对方走去。

sentences.en: They do this sort of goose-stepping, like high-kicking march towards each other.
sentences.zh: 他们以一种非常阳刚的方式握手。

sentences.en: They shake hands in a very manly fashion.
sentences.zh: 他们打开大门。

sentences.en: They open the gates.
sentences.zh: 他们猛地关上大门。

sentences.en: They slam the gates.
sentences.zh: 有很多当地人来看这个表演。

sentences.en: And there's lots of people who go to this, mostly locals, I understand, and watch.
sentences.zh: 在平常的日子里，这里的体育场座无虚席。

sentences.en: On a typical day, the stadiums here are full.
sentences.zh: 这是该地区最受欢迎的边境口岸。

sentences.en: This is the most popular border crossing in the region.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它是旅游杂志上经常报道的那个。

sentences.en: As in, it's the one often written about in tourism magazines.
sentences.zh: 但这些军事表演发生在分隔印度和巴基斯坦的漫长锯齿状边境线的各个点上。

sentences.en: But these military performances take place at various points along the long, jagged line
sentences.zh: 这条线本身就有一段相当离奇的历史。

sentences.en: that separates India and Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子，说明大多数国界是如何以相当随机、草率的方式创建的。

sentences.en: A line which itself has a pretty bizarre history.
sentences.zh: 这就是在英国几个世纪的帝国统治之后，分裂这些国家的分割线。

sentences.en: It's an example of how most national borders were created in pretty random, haphazard ways.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战让英国变得一贫如洗。

sentences.en: This was the line of partition that divided these nations after, you know, centuries of imperial rule by the British.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定放弃一些殖民项目，包括英属印度。

sentences.en: World War II left the British kind of broke.
sentences.zh: 计划是在其后建立两个新国家：印度和巴基斯坦。

sentences.en: So they decided to abandon a number of their colonial projects, including British India.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是划分两个国家，同时进行的项目的一部分是试图专门按宗教来划分这两个国家。

sentences.en: The plan was to form two new countries in their wake, India and Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 概念是该地区的印度教人口将进入印度，

sentences.en: It wasn't just demarcating the two countries, but part of the project that was happening at the same time
sentences.zh: 而穆斯林人口将进入巴基斯坦。

sentences.en: was trying to divide the two countries specifically by religion.
sentences.zh: 英国人指派一个人，西里尔·拉德克利夫爵士，负责划定界线并创建这两个国家。

sentences.en: The concept was that the Hindu population of this region would go into India
sentences.zh: 拉德克利夫是一位英国律师。

sentences.en: and the Muslim population would go into Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 尽管他被宣布为划分这两个新国家的权威，

sentences.en: The British charged one man, Sir Cyril Radcliffe, with the task of drawing the line and creating the two nations.
sentences.zh: 但他对该地区几乎一无所知，也从未去过那里。

sentences.en: Radcliffe was a British lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他知道的几乎为零，也从未访问过。

sentences.en: And although he was declared the authority on carving out these two new countries,
sentences.zh: 尽管他被宣布为划分这两个新国家的权威，

sentences.en: he knew next to nothing about the region and had never visited.
sentences.zh: 他几乎对该地区一无所知，也从未访问过。

sentences.en: Following nationalist riots in India, the British wanted to speed up their departure in 1947.
sentences.zh: 1947年，在印度发生民族主义骚乱后，英国人希望加快撤离的步伐。

sentences.en: And so, Radcliffe was given just five weeks to draw the new border.
sentences.zh: 于是，拉德克利夫只被给了五周时间来划定新的边界。

sentences.en: That wasn't enough time for him to even get his hands on an updated map.
sentences.zh: 这点时间甚至不够他拿到一份最新的地图。

sentences.en: And even though Britain intended to divide the countries along religious lines,
sentences.zh: 尽管英国打算按照宗教界线来划分这两个国家，

sentences.en: Muslims, Hindus, and Sikhs had lived for centuries side by side, all throughout the region.
sentences.zh: 但穆斯林、印度教徒和锡克教徒几个世纪以来一直在这片地区比邻而居。

sentences.en: He, you know, studied maps and consulted some people,
sentences.zh: 他研究了地图，也咨询了一些人，

sentences.en: but he was given very short time to do this homework and almost willy-nilly just drew this line.
sentences.zh: 但他完成这项任务的时间非常仓促，几乎是随心所欲地画下了这条线。

sentences.en: Ultimately, the Radcliffe line was drawn and the British declared an independent India and Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 最终，拉德克利夫线被画了出来，英国宣布印度和巴基斯坦独立。

sentences.en: Fearing mass protest, exact information of where the line would be was released to the public
sentences.zh: 由于担心大规模抗议，关于边界确切位置的信息直到

sentences.en: two days after the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 独立宣言发布两天后才向公众公布。

sentences.en: This meant that millions of people celebrated independence without even knowing which country they were in.
sentences.zh: 这意味着数百万人在庆祝独立时，甚至不知道自己身处哪个国家。

sentences.en: Some towns raised both the Pakistani and Indian flags.
sentences.zh: 有些城镇同时升起了巴基斯坦和印度的国旗。

sentences.en: But once word of the line had spread, millions suddenly became a religious minority,
sentences.zh: 但一旦边界线的消息传开，数百万人的身份突然变成了宗教少数派，

sentences.en: if they were Hindu or Sikh, living in the area that became Pakistan,
sentences.zh: 如果他们是居住在后来成为巴基斯坦地区的印度教徒或锡克教徒，

sentences.en: or if they were Muslim, living in the area that became India.
sentences.zh: 或者他们是居住在后来成为印度地区的穆斯林。

sentences.en: And for many of those people, that celebration quickly turned into horror.
sentences.zh: 对其中许多人来说，那种庆祝很快就变成了噩梦。

sentences.en: The amount of violence that occurred almost instantly was incredible.
sentences.zh: 几乎瞬间爆发的暴力事件令人难以置信。

sentences.en: People were driven out of their homes and were subject to mass communal violence and rioting.
sentences.zh: 人们被赶出家园，遭受大规模的群体暴力和骚乱。

sentences.en: I think the highest estimate is around 2 million people died as a direct result of this partition.
sentences.zh: 我认为最高估计约有200万人因这次分治直接丧生。

sentences.en: Cyril Radcliffe's line, that smooth stroke of pen,
sentences.zh: 西里尔·拉德克利夫画下的那条线，那轻描淡写的一笔，

sentences.en: it suddenly put about 15 million people in the wrong place,
sentences.zh: 突然让大约1500万人处于错误的位置，

sentences.en: making it the largest forced migration in the world.
sentences.zh: 使其成为世界上最大规模的被迫移民事件。

sentences.en: This is one of the most stark examples, but there's so many throughout the world.
sentences.zh: 这是最鲜明的例子之一，但全世界还有很多这样的例子。

sentences.en: If you look at the current way that the world is divided into nation states,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看当今世界划分民族国家的方式，

sentences.en: over 40% of all borders were drawn by Britain and France.
sentences.zh: 超过40%的边界是由英国和法国划定的。

sentences.en: They were just drawn on a map and imposed upon the populations.
sentences.zh: 它们只是在地图上画出来，然后强加给当地民众。

sentences.en: And sometimes that, you know, kind of works out or doesn't have a huge effect.
sentences.zh: 有时，你知道，这可能行得通，或者不会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: But in the case of India and Pakistan, I mean, the effects were devastating
sentences.zh: 但在印度和巴基斯坦的案例中，我的意思是，其影响是毁灭性的，

sentences.en: and truly, I think, hard to grasp.
sentences.zh: 而且说实话，我认为很难理解。

sentences.en: It's telling that after drawing the line, Radcliffe burned all of his paperwork.
sentences.zh: 耐人寻味的是，在划定边界线后，拉德克利夫烧毁了他所有的文书。

sentences.en: He left India and even declined to receive payment from the British government for the job.
sentences.zh: 他离开了印度，甚至拒绝接受英国政府支付的报酬。

sentences.en: Much of the India-Pakistan border is fenced and lit up by the Indian government.
sentences.zh: 印巴边界的大部分地区都被印度政府设置了围栏并安装了照明。

sentences.en: 1,200 miles of bright floodlights making the line visible from outer space.
sentences.zh: 1200英里长的明亮泛光灯，使得这条边界线在太空中清晰可见。

sentences.en: It's one of the most contested borders in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是世界上争议最激烈的边界之一。

sentences.en: And yet, the Atarivaga border crossing can also be a place to have a picnic and watch some circus-like fun.
sentences.zh: 然而，阿塔里-瓦加边境口岸也可以是一个野餐和观看马戏表演的地方。

sentences.en: It's an absolute contradiction.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个矛盾。

sentences.en: One that John says isn't so unusual.
sentences.zh: 约翰说，这种矛盾并不罕见。

sentences.en: And much like this border, John says all borders are selectively permeable.
sentences.zh: 就像这条边界一样，约翰说所有的边界都是有选择地渗透的。

sentences.en: They are closed down to certain people, but they are very open to the flows of capital, to the trading of arms, all sorts of other things.
sentences.zh: 它们对某些人关闭，但对资本流动、武器贸易以及各种其他事物却非常开放。

sentences.en: So there's always that sort of dissonance and always that clash at every borderline throughout the world.
sentences.zh: 所以世界上每一条边界线上总是存在那种不和谐和冲突。

sentences.en: It's in Kashmir where the Radcliffe Line stops.
sentences.zh: 拉德克利夫线在克什米尔地区终止。

sentences.en: The British left that disputed territory for India and Pakistan to resolve on their own in 1947.
sentences.zh: 1947年，英国人将那片有争议的领土留给印度和巴基斯坦自行解决。

sentences.en: And they immediately went to war over it.
sentences.zh: 他们随即为此爆发了战争。

sentences.en: Lately, a war over borders is once again at the center of conflict between the two nuclear-armed countries.
sentences.zh: 最近，一场关于边界的战争再次成为这两个拥核国家冲突的焦点。

sentences.en: And for 12 days, the daily theatrical rivalry at this border crossing was put on pause.
sentences.zh: 在这12天里，这个边境口岸每天上演的仪式化对抗被暂停了。

sentences.en: The performance has since resumed, but now with some key changes.
sentences.zh: 表演后来恢复了，但现在有了一些关键的变化。

sentences.en: This time, the gates do not open.
sentences.zh: 这一次，大门没有打开。

sentences.en: And there is no handshake.
sentences.zh: 也没有握手仪式。

sentences.en: We'll be back after this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We're back with producer Lasha Madon.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了制片人拉莎·马登身边。

sentences.en: A border is a line that can shift and bend, and is often a lot less rigid than we might think.
sentences.zh: 边界是一条可以移动和弯曲的线，通常比我们想象的要灵活得多。

sentences.en: John Washington, author of the book The Case for Open Borders,
sentences.zh: 《开放边界的理由》一书的作者约翰·华盛顿，

sentences.en: writes that if history is any guide, national borders are always moving,
sentences.zh: 写道，如果历史可以作为参考，国家边界总是在移动，

sentences.en: often conveniently closing shut behind those who enforce them.
sentences.zh: 而且往往会方便地在那些执行边界政策的人身后关闭。

sentences.en: With that, we've arrived at our third stop, Australia, 2001.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，我们来到了第三站，2001年的澳大利亚。

sentences.en: There's a really momentous case, both in international law and for Australia itself, in 2001.
sentences.zh: 2001年发生了一起在国际法和澳大利亚自身历史上都非常重大的案件。

sentences.en: A small fishing boat crammed with 433 asylum seekers was on its way to Australia
sentences.zh: 一艘挤满了433名寻求庇护者的小渔船正在前往澳大利亚的途中，

sentences.en: when the boat's engine failed in international waters.
sentences.zh: 当时船只的引擎在公海发生故障。

sentences.en: The people aboard, who were mostly from Afghanistan, were rescued by a nearby container ship.
sentences.zh: 船上的人大多来自阿富汗，被附近的一艘集装箱船救起。

sentences.en: The ship's captain was shocked by the health conditions of some people aboard,
sentences.zh: 船长对船上一些人的健康状况感到震惊，

sentences.en: and he began to sail to the closest port for safety.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始驶向最近的港口以寻求安全。

sentences.en: And they ended up on Christmas Island, which is an island about 1,000 miles off the coast of mainland Australia,
sentences.zh: 他们最终到达了圣诞岛，这是一个距离澳大利亚大陆约1000英里的岛屿，

sentences.en: but is claimed by the country of Australia.
sentences.zh: 但被澳大利亚宣称拥有主权。

sentences.en: And so when they got to Christmas Island, they were not allowed to dock,
sentences.zh: 所以当他们到达圣诞岛时，他们不被允许靠岸，

sentences.en: because Australia was really nervous about the fact that if they touched land,
sentences.zh: 因为澳大利亚非常担心，如果他们踏上陆地，

sentences.en: they would be able to levy an asylum claim.
sentences.zh: 他们就能够提出庇护申请。

sentences.en: And they would have to welcome them in, hear out their claims,
sentences.zh: 而澳大利亚将不得不接纳他们，听取他们的申请，

sentences.en: and then maybe even grant them if they were legitimate.
sentences.zh: 如果申请合法，甚至可能批准他们入境。

sentences.en: So the asylum seekers waited in limbo.
sentences.zh: 于是，这些寻求庇护者陷入了困境。

sentences.en: They remained on board the vessel near Christmas Island,
sentences.zh: 他们留在圣诞岛附近的船上，

sentences.en: while the Australian government argued over their fate.
sentences.zh: 而澳大利亚政府则在争论他们的命运。

sentences.en: Their conditions grew more and more bleak.
sentences.zh: 他们的处境变得越来越凄凉。

sentences.en: Some of the migrants began a hunger strike.
sentences.zh: 一些移民开始绝食抗议。

sentences.en: People were sick.
sentences.zh: 人们生病了。

sentences.en: People were on the verge of dying.
sentences.zh: 人们濒临死亡。

sentences.en: The ship's captain kept trying to get Australia's attention.
sentences.zh: 船长一直试图引起澳大利亚的注意。

sentences.en: On the fourth, desperate day, he started sailing towards mainland Australia.
sentences.zh: 在绝望的第四天，他开始驶向澳大利亚大陆。

sentences.en: A high-sea standoff with the captain of a Norwegian freighter,
sentences.zh: 这是一场与挪威货轮船长的公海对峙，

sentences.en: who picked up more than 400 asylum seekers from a sinking boat
sentences.zh: 他从一艘正在下沉的船上救起了400多名寻求庇护者，

sentences.en: and attempted to enter Australian waters.
sentences.zh: 并试图进入澳大利亚水域。

sentences.en: The government refused, deploying SAS troops in a show of military force.
sentences.zh: 政府拒绝了，并部署了特种空勤团（SAS）进行军事威慑。

sentences.en: Besides sending military to prevent the ship from sailing any closer,
sentences.zh: 除了派遣军队阻止船只进一步靠近外，

sentences.en: the Australian government got to work,
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚政府还采取了行动，

sentences.en: quickly passing the first of a series of laws,
sentences.zh: 迅速通过了一系列法律中的第一部，

sentences.en: suddenly giving them the power to refuse entry to asylum seekers arriving by boat.
sentences.zh: 突然赋予他们拒绝乘船抵达的寻求庇护者入境的权力。

sentences.en: And this is an example of what is called a turnback.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“遣返”的一个例子。

sentences.en: Australia redirected the asylum seekers to other islands,
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚将这些寻求庇护者重新引导到其他岛屿，

sentences.en: including a tiny island country called Nauru.
sentences.zh: 包括一个叫瑙鲁的小岛国。

sentences.en: Which is this guano-covered, incredibly hot, isolated island,
sentences.zh: 这是一个覆盖着鸟粪、极其炎热、与世隔绝的岛屿，

sentences.en: where they detained these asylum seekers.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里拘留了这些寻求庇护者。

sentences.en: Nauru was once a country rich in natural resources.
sentences.zh: 瑙鲁曾经是一个自然资源丰富的国家。

sentences.en: But after being mined by a series of corrupt governments,
sentences.zh: 但在被历届腐败政府开采后，

sentences.en: it was left desperate for money.
sentences.zh: 它变得极度缺钱。

sentences.en: And so, when Australia approached them and said,
sentences.zh: 所以，当澳大利亚找到他们并说，

sentences.en: we want to build a detention center on your land,
sentences.zh: 我们想在你们的土地上建立一个拘留中心，

sentences.en: it wasn't really in a position to refuse.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有拒绝的余地。

sentences.en: Refugees trying to get to Australia would be redirected to Nauru
sentences.zh: 试图前往澳大利亚的难民会被重新引导到瑙鲁，

sentences.en: and have their applications for asylum to Australia processed there.
sentences.zh: 并在那里处理他们向澳大利亚提出的庇护申请。

sentences.en: And what they decided to do, besides deflect their claim,
sentences.zh: 他们决定做的，除了拒绝他们的申请外，

sentences.en: is imprison them.
sentences.zh: 就是监禁他们。

sentences.en: Actually, this is the first establishment of a detention center
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是第一个在离岸岛屿上建立的拘留中心，

sentences.en: on this, like, offshore island.
sentences.zh: 这种做法澳大利亚一直沿用至今。

sentences.en: And this is a practice that Australia has been doing ever since.
sentences.zh: 起初只是对2001年那艘船抵达的仓促政治回应，

sentences.en: What began as a hurried political response to the arrival of that one boat in 2001
sentences.zh: 后来发展成了一系列永久性的移民政策。

sentences.en: grew into a series of permanent immigration policies.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚将这套新法律称为“太平洋解决方案”。

sentences.en: Australia called this new set of laws the Pacific Solution.
sentences.zh: “太平洋解决方案”还涉及其他内容。

sentences.en: The Pacific Solution involved something else, too.
sentences.zh: 一些相当极端的内容。

sentences.en: Something kind of extreme.
sentences.zh: 他们决定做的是将圣诞岛，

sentences.en: And what they decided to do was actually to excise Christmas Island,
sentences.zh: 以及其他几个岛屿，从澳大利亚官方领土中剔除。

sentences.en: as well as a few other islands, from official Australian national territory.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，如果未来有任何阿富汗人或其他任何人到达圣诞岛，

sentences.en: So that way, if any Afghani or any other person made it to Christmas Island in the future,
sentences.zh: 他们就不能申请庇护。

sentences.en: they couldn't ask for asylum.
sentences.zh: 就这样，澳大利亚的边界被改变了。

sentences.en: Just like that, the Australian border was changed.
sentences.zh: 这项新政策被追溯到难民进入澳大利亚水域前两个半小时生效。

sentences.en: The new policy was backdated to two and a half hours
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，这些人抵达澳大利亚的官方记忆被抹去了。

sentences.en: before the refugees entered Australian waters.
sentences.zh: 这些寻求庇护者从未真正踏入过澳大利亚。

sentences.en: This way, the official memory of the arrival of those people to Australia had been erased.
sentences.zh: 至少，没有以任何对他们有利的方式踏入过。

sentences.en: The asylum seekers had never really been in Australia at all.
sentences.zh: 总的观点是，

sentences.en: At least, not in any way that could be of benefit to them.
sentences.zh: 那些试图阻挡移民的人谈论边界的方式，

sentences.en: The broad point is that
sentences.zh: 是将其视为不可动摇、神圣不可侵犯的界线，

sentences.en: the way that people who are trying to keep away migrants
sentences.zh: 深深植根于历史之中。

sentences.en: talk about borders is that they are these
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: immovable, psychosanct lines
sentences.zh: 它们是可塑的。

sentences.en: that are deeply rooted in history.
sentences.zh: 而且它们一直在被移动。

sentences.en: But they're not.
sentences.zh: 我认为澳大利亚为了保护其边界而愿意移动其边界，

sentences.en: They are malleable.
sentences.zh: 是一个非常有说明意义的例子。

sentences.en: And they are constantly being moved.
sentences.zh: 2001年事件发生后，

sentences.en: And that Australia was willing to
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛上也建起了一个拘留中心。

sentences.en: move its border to protect its border,
sentences.zh: 它被称为拥有1亿只螃蟹自由漫步的岛屿。

sentences.en: I think, is a really telling example.
sentences.zh: 但难民却生活在铁窗之后。

sentences.en: After the 2001 incident,
sentences.zh: 在《开放边界的理由》一书中，

sentences.en: a detention center was built on Christmas Island, too.
sentences.zh: 这就是约翰·华盛顿的论点。

sentences.en: It became known as the island on which 100 million crabs roam free.
sentences.zh: 人们应该能够随心所欲地移动和迁徙。

sentences.en: But refugees live behind bars.
sentences.zh: 与其将越境的人定为罪犯，

sentences.en: In The Case for Open Borders,
sentences.zh: 我们更应该担心的是这样一个社会：我们拒绝向绝望的人提供援助，

sentences.en: this is John Washington's argument.
sentences.zh: 让他们被困在沙漠公路边，

sentences.en: People should be able to move and migrate wherever they want and need to.
sentences.zh: 就像约翰多年前在安扎-博雷戈沙漠中对待那个年轻人一样。

sentences.en: That instead of criminalizing people for crossing a border,
sentences.zh: 说得更简单一点，

sentences.en: we should instead fear the society in which we deny a desperate person aid,
sentences.zh: 约翰说我们应该开放边界。

sentences.en: leaving them stranded on the side of a desert road,
sentences.zh: 开放边界并不意味着没有边界。

sentences.en: much like John did with that young man years ago in the Anza Borrego desert.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为在社区周围划定某种界线是有意义的，

sentences.en: To put it even more simply,
sentences.zh: 你可以说这些人属于这个共同体，

sentences.en: John says we should open our borders.
sentences.zh: 而那些人属于另一个共同体。

sentences.en: Open borders is not no borders.
sentences.zh: 我认为那只是，你知道，政治组织方式。

sentences.en: I do think it makes sense to draw some sort of line around a community
sentences.zh: 但在我所说的开放边界版本中，

sentences.en: in which you say that these people are part of this commonwealth
sentences.zh: 前提是，

sentences.en: and these people are part of the other.
sentences.zh: 那条线是可以跨越的。

sentences.en: I think that's just, you know, political organizing.
sentences.zh: 这只是政治组织。

sentences.en: But the presumption would be,
sentences.zh: 但前提是，

sentences.en: in the version of open borders I'm talking about,
sentences.zh: 在我所说的开放边界版本中，

sentences.en: that that line can be crossed.
sentences.zh: 那条线是可以跨越的。

sentences.en: And anyone can do it.
sentences.zh: 而且任何人都可以做到。

sentences.en: And they don't need a compelling reason to do so.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不需要什么令人信服的理由。

sentences.en: This idea might sound radical now.
sentences.zh: 这个想法现在听起来可能很激进。

sentences.en: But it wasn't always that way.
sentences.zh: 但情况并非一直如此。

sentences.en: Even Ronald Reagan called for what sounds like an open border
sentences.zh: 甚至罗纳德·里根在1980年的共和党总统初选辩论中，

sentences.en: between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 也曾呼吁建立一种听起来像是开放边界的政策，

sentences.en: and Mexico
sentences.zh: 就在美国

sentences.en: at a Republican presidential primary debate in 1980.
sentences.zh: 和墨西哥之间。

sentences.en: Rather than making them,
sentences.zh: 与其制造他们，
